name: context-copy-search
description: Search text across workspace files, preview results, and copy full containing functions/classes with source annotations.

commands.title: Context Copy Search: Search and Copy Contexts

viewsWelcome.contents:
Preview workspace matches, or search and immediately copy containing functions/classes with source annotations.
[Preview Matches](command:contextCopySearch.previewMatches) · [Search and Copy Contexts](command:contextCopySearch.searchAndCopy)

contextCopySearch.includeGlob.description: Comma-separated glob(s) of files to search. Empty means all searchable workspace files, closest to normal VS Code Search.

contextCopySearch.excludeGlob.description: Comma-separated extra glob(s) to exclude. Empty is recommended; VS Code search.exclude/files.exclude and ignore-file settings are mirrored separately.

contextCopySearch.maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to scan.

contextCopySearch.maxMatches.description: Maximum number of matches to collect. This is a safety cap; increase it for very large searches.

contextCopySearch.maxFileBytes.description: Skip files larger than this many bytes.

contextCopySearch.fallbackContextLines.description: Lines before/after a match when no function/class can be inferred.

contextCopySearch.useVSCodeSearch.description: Deprecated setting kept for compatibility. It is ignored; this extension now avoids VS Code proposed APIs.

contextCopySearch.respectIgnoreFiles.description: When using ripgrep, respect .gitignore, .ignore, global ignore files, and parent ignore files.

contextCopySearch.searchEngine.description: Search engine to use. auto prefers bundled ripgrep, then ripgrep from PATH, then the slow fallback scanner. No VS Code proposed APIs are used.

contextCopySearch.searchHidden.description: When using ripgrep, include hidden files and directories. Keep false to behave closer to normal VS Code Search.

contextCopySearch.insertMatchMarkers.description: Insert comment markers above every matching source line inside copied context blocks, so every individual occurrence is visible even when multiple matches share one function/class.
